section_summary: This section contains November 1947 statistics on communicable and venereal diseases in Japan, followed by a 1948 technical bulletin describing the Ministry of Welfare and prefectural welfare administration. Later documents report a Rockefeller Foundation survey of public health, population growth, and birth control, and transmit another SCAP public health report.

subfiles.title: Number of Cases and Deaths of Communicable Diseases for Comparable Period, 1946 and 1947
subfiles.about: Compares reported communicable disease cases, deaths, and rates in 1946 and 1947.
subfiles.summary: Tables compare weekly, four-week, and cumulative disease figures and rates.

subfiles.title: Weekly Summary Report of Venereal Diseases in Japan
subfiles.about: Reports chancroid, gonorrhea, and syphilis cases by prefecture.
subfiles.summary: Lists current and year-to-date cases for three venereal diseases.

subfiles.title: Digest of Monthly Report of Communicable Diseases in Japan
subfiles.about: Reviews communicable disease trends during the five-week period ending November 29, 1947.
subfiles.summary: The digest reports 6,400 cases and 881 deaths among twelve diseases, with diphtheria, typhoid, and dysentery accounting for most. Prefectural tables give cases, deaths, and rates for each disease and compare November 1947 with October 1947 and November 1946. The report also corrects selected October figures.

subfiles.title: Organization Plan to be Adopted by the Ministry of Welfare
subfiles.from: Office of the United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits a technical bulletin on Japanese health, welfare, and social insurance administration.
subfiles.summary: Encloses Sections I and II of a Public Health and Welfare technical bulletin.

subfiles.title: Administration of Health, Welfare and Social Insurance in Japan: Section I, Ministry of Welfare
subfiles.from: Public Health and Welfare Section, GHQ SCAP
subfiles.about: Describes the national Ministry of Welfare’s organization, history, and bureau responsibilities.
subfiles.summary: The bulletin explains the Ministry’s public health, medical affairs, disease prevention, social affairs, children’s, insurance, repatriation, and demobilization functions. It traces changes in these bureaus and their relationships with prefectural administration. An organization chart closes the section.

subfiles.title: Administration of Health, Welfare and Social Insurance in Japan: Section II, Public Welfare and Social Insurance
subfiles.from: Public Health and Welfare Section, GHQ SCAP
subfiles.about: Sets out a model for prefectural and local welfare and social insurance administration.
subfiles.summary: Section II assigns responsibilities to prefectural welfare departments and their social affairs, protection, children’s, insurance, and demobilization sections. It discusses child welfare centers, insurance offices, and city, town, and village administration. Charts show administrative relationships, and an annex lists Japan’s cities with populations over 100,000 in the 1947 census.

subfiles.title: Rockefeller Foundation Survey of Inter-related Problems of Public Health and Demography in Japan
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits and summarizes a conversation with Frank W. Notestein about Japan’s population outlook.
subfiles.summary: Sebald reports Notestein’s projection of a population near 120 million by 1970, his concerns about food supply, and possible Rockefeller Foundation support for demographic research. He also summarizes Notestein’s views on Japanese-led birth control and notes Edward A. Ackerman’s differing projection.

subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation with Dr. Frank W. Notestein
subfiles.about: Records Notestein’s assessment of Japanese population growth and proposals for demographic research.
subfiles.summary: Notestein discusses a possible population of 120 million, the limited land available to support it, and divided responsibility among Occupation sections. He argues that Japanese people want birth-control information, while sponsorship should remain Japanese. The survey group considers fellowships, expert exchanges, improved demographic studies, and private distribution of technical information.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Report Prepared by Public Health and Welfare Section of General Headquarters, SCAP
subfiles.from: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits a SCAP report on occupation health and welfare work through July 31, 1948.
subfiles.summary: Encloses one copy of Public Health and Welfare in Japan with accompanying charts.
